title: Generation of hematopoietic lineage cell-specific chimeric mice using retrovirus-transduced fetal liver cells
protocol: Seed 2.5 × 10^6 Platinum-E (Plat-E) retroviral packaging cells in 100 mm cell culture plates.
Add 10 mL of DMEM media with 10% FBS to the cell culture plates.
Incubate the cells in a 5% CO2 incubator at 37°C for approximately 15 hours.
Warm serum-free DMEM medium in a 37°C water bath for at least 15 minutes.
Allow the vial of FuGENE® HD transfection reagent to reach approximately 25°C.
Add 4.5 μg of retroviral vector and 1.5 μg of pCL-Eco helper plasmid to pre-warmed medium to achieve a final volume of 600 μL.
Vortex the tubes containing the plasmids and transfection reagents.
Spin down the contents of the tubes.
Add 18 μL of FuGENE® HD transfection reagent directly to the medium and mix immediately by tapping the tube.
Incubate the mixture for 15 minutes at approximately 25°C.
Carefully add the mixture to the plated cells in a dropwise manner.
Mix gently.
Return cells to the incubator for 48 hours.
Measure transfection efficiency using the GFP signal after 24 hours.
Harvest the cell supernatant containing the retrovirus on Day 4, timing approximately 30 minutes.
Filter through a 0.45 μm filter.
Use only cellulose acetate or polyethersulfone filters.
Add 10 mL of fresh DMEM 10% (v/v) FBS medium to the plated cells.
Return cells to the incubator for 24 hours.
Transfer clarified supernatant to a sterile 15 mL conical tube.
Combine 3 mL of Retro-X Concentrator with 9 mL of clarified supernatant.
Mix by gentle inversion.
Incubate mixture at 4°C for approximately 15 hours.
Concentrate the retrovirus-containing supernatant according to the manufacturer's protocol.
Incubate the retroviral supernatant with Retro-X concentrator.
Centrifuge the mixture at 1,500 × g for 45 min at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant carefully without disturbing the pellet.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL DMEM 20% (v/v) FBS medium supplemented with antibiotics.
Filter the retrovirus-containing supernatant through a 0.45 μm filter.
Repeat steps 11 and 12 for the second harvest of retroviral supernatant.
Concentrate the second harvest of retroviral supernatant according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Repeat steps 13–15 for the second concentration of retroviral supernatant.
Euthanize pregnant mice by CO2 inhalation.
Harvest E15.5 embryos and place them in PBS in a 100 mm cell culture dish on ice.
Separate the embryos from the uterus.
Transfer the embryos to a new dish with PBS.
Swirl the dish to remove blood from the embryos.
Euthanize embryos by decapitation.
Dissect liver tissues.
Place liver tissues in a 24-well cell culture plate with 1 mL DMEM 10% (v/v) FBS medium.
Cut a section of the tail for genotyping and place it in an Eppendorf microcentrifuge tube.
Squeeze livers through a 45 μm cell strainer using the end of a 1 mL plastic syringe.
Resuspend liver samples in 10 mL DMEM 10% (v/v) FBS medium.
Spin down cells at 300 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend cells in 1 mL RBC lysis buffer.
Incubate the cell suspension for 1 min at approximately 25°C.
Stop the lysis reaction by adding 5 mL DMEM 10% (v/v) FBS medium.
Resuspend the cell pellet completely using a 1000 μL pipette.
Filter 6 mL of the cell suspension through a 40 μm pore nylon mesh.
Spin down cells at 300 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend cells in 1 mL DMEM 20% (v/v) FBS medium supplemented with antibiotics.
Count the cells using a hemocytometer.

Plate fetal liver cells at a density of 4 × 10^7 cells per 150 mm cell culture dish in 15 mL of DMEM 20% (v/v) FBS medium supplemented with antibiotics, IL-3 (20 ng/mL), IL-6 (50 ng/mL), and SCF (50 ng/mL).
Incubate fetal liver cells at 37°C with 5% CO2 for 24 h.
Add 300 μL of 50 mM NaOH to the tail biopsy and dissolve completely in a heat block at 97°C for 1 h.
Neutralize by adding 50 μL of 1 M Tris-HCl buffer (pH 8.0).
Centrifuge the samples at 11,500 × g at 4°C for 6 min.
Prepare a cocktail of PCR reagents for each mouse to be analyzed.
Add 1 μL of tail DNA to 11 μL of the prepared cocktail.
Briefly vortex the mixture and spin down.
Perform PCR using the appropriate thermal cycling conditions.
Analyze products of the amplification reaction using electrophoresis through an agarose gel to verify the genotype.
Obtain embryos via cesarean section from female mice on day 15.5 of gestation.
Isolate the liver from the embryos.
Obtain a single-cell suspension of the liver cells.
Lysate the red blood cells in the suspension.
Stabilize the cells in media supplemented with IL-3, IL-6, and SCF.
Harvest fetal liver cells cultured for 24 hours from 150 mm cell culture plates by pipetting into a sterile 50 mL conical tube.
Wash the plates vigorously with 10 mL of PBS and collect into the conical tube.
Repeat washing to harvest as many cells as possible.
Centrifuge the cells at 300 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant from the centrifuged cells.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL DMEM supplemented with 20% FBS and antibiotics.
Count the resuspended cells.
Resuspend 3 × 10^6 cells per 1 mL of DMEM supplemented with 20% FBS, antibiotics, IL-3 (40 ng/mL), IL-6 (100 ng/mL), and SCF (100 ng/mL).
Reconstitute retroviral supernatant with 5 mL of DMEM 20% (v/v) FBS medium supplemented with antibiotics and polybrene.
Mix the reconstituted retroviral supernatant with fetal liver cell suspension in a 1:1 (v/v) ratio.
Transfer 2 mL of the mixture to each well of a 6-well tissue culture plate.
Spin the wrapped 6-well plates at 1,000 × g for 60 min at 37°C.
Remove plastic wrap and place the plates in a 5% CO2 incubator at 37°C for 24 h.
Add 5 mL of DMEM 20% (v/v) FBS medium supplemented with antibiotics, IL-3, IL-6, SCF, and polybrene to 1 mL of concentrated retroviral supernatant.
Carefully add 1 mL of the retroviral supernatant mixture to each well containing fetal liver cells incubated for 24 h.
Wrap the plate with plastic wrap and repeat spin infection at 37°C at 1,000 × g for 60 min.
Unwrap the plate and incubate in a 5% CO2 incubator at 37°C for 24 h.
Add fresh supplemented DMEM to maintain fetal liver cells in healthy condition.
After 24 h, carefully remove the top 2 mL of medium from each well of the 6-well plate containing the fetal liver cells, leaving only 1 mL of medium.
Place the tip on the edge and carefully aspirate the supernatant to avoid sucking up fetal liver cells.
Spin down at 300 × g for 5 min at 4°C to prevent loss of fetal liver cells before removing the top 2 mL of medium.
Add 1 mL of fresh DMEM 20% (v/v) FBS medium supplemented with antibiotics, IL-3 (20 ng/mL), IL-6 (50 ng/mL), and SCF (50 ng/mL) to each well of the 6-well plate.
Incubate the cells in a 5% CO2 incubator at 37°C for 24 h.
Irradiate recipient mice with 4 Gy from an X-ray or gamma-irradiator the day before injection of fetal liver cells.
Harvest transduced fetal liver cells for transplantation into irradiated recipient mice.
Incubate fetal liver cells for 24 hours.
Collect fetal liver cells from 6-well plates by pipetting after washing vigorously with PBS.
Repeat washing step to harvest as many cells as possible.
Centrifuge the collected cells at 300 × g at 4°C for 10 minutes.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the fetal liver cells in 1 mL of RPMI-1640 medium supplemented with antibiotics.
Keep the cells on ice.
Take a 10 μL sample to count the cells using a hemocytometer.
Resuspend the cells in RPMI-1640 medium supplemented with antibiotics at a concentration of 0.5–1 × 10^7 cells/mL.
Incubate FBS at 56°C for 30 minutes to inactivate components of the complement system and other potentially unknown cell growth inhibitors.
Take a 10 μL sample from each set of fetal liver cells and analyze transduction efficiency using flow cytometry based on GFP expression.
Transduce fetal liver cells.
Adoptively transfer transduced fetal liver cells into recipient mice.
Euthanize chimeric mice six weeks after cell transfer.
Analyze immune cells via flow cytometry.
Load 200 μL of fetal liver cells per mouse into a 1/2 cc short needle insulin syringe (30-gauge).
Heat the mice using an infrared lamp.
Intravenously inject 200 μL of fetal liver cells per mouse via a tail vein.
Monitor the mice weekly to ensure they remain healthy.
Collect a small amount of blood from each mouse after five to six weeks.
Confirm reconstitution of immune cells derived from injected fetal liver cells using flow cytometry based on GFP expression.
Sacrifice recipient mice.
Analyze cells from lymphoid organs using flow cytometry.
